references.text: Here the same objects are mentioned - the carved image, the ephod, the teraphim and the cast image - that Micah made for his idolatrous house.
The spies report on the same cultic objects in Micah's house - the ephod, the teraphim, the carved image and the cast image.
Describes how the five men went in to take the carved image, the ephod, the teraphim and the cast image.
The priest took the ephod, the teraphim and the carved image and went with the people, showing that he accepted the theft.
The first description of the ephod as a sacred priestly garment, which shows the context for this cultic object.
Rachel stole the teraphim from her father Laban, showing that the teraphim were household gods used in idolatry.
Hosea prophesies that Israel will be without an ephod and teraphim, showing the significance of these objects in Israelite religion.
